release_review.summary: Redeven v0.12.0 replaces the private Desktop placement frame multiplexer with one bounded HTTP/2 session over the existing authenticated stdio exec while preserving Runtime lifecycle ownership and the separate Flowersec private-loopback boundary at compatibility epoch 10.
checked_surfaces: DeepSeek uses the published Floret stateless Responses gateway, fixed Agent hosted search, and existing supplemental-context privacy fences without changing the Desktop or Runtime protocol. Redeven consumes published github.com/floegence/floret/v7 v7.4.0 with GOWORK=off and exact module checksums; every production Agent binds one immutable RunLabels snapshot at construction so fresh execution and continuations share Floret's provider-host injection point, while provider admission and policy refresh never rebind the admitted permission snapshot; committed final provider usage carries canonical whole-thread cache token totals through the live event boundary without a downstream ledger, while projected requests preserve the last confirmed totals; Floret-native web_fetch owns secure public-text fetching, parsing, output policy, and typed Activity with a bounded preview while ignoring page icons, and Redeven owns current product authorization plus one Searching indicator that animates only while the fetch is running; runtime startup atomically converges legacy UTF-8 tool-result Raw data, exact RunID identity, and every dispatching, retrying, or unknown effect into one typed terminal failure before the Host is available and removes terminal forked Effect Attempt history only when source-thread ancestry and execution identity are verified; canonical Effect results converge from one committed entry with valid UTF-8 text, segmented records preserve active-turn recovery without whole-state rewrites, published SQLite maintenance reclaims eligible free pages before the single runtime open, root inventory supplies summary-only list projection, cumulative typed Activity preserves terminal call descriptions through results and restart, additive terminal operation and safe byte/cursor facts keep every terminal call inspectable without exposing interactive input, user cancellation binds the selected Turn’s current Run atomically with settlement, typed SubAgent operation Activity preserves the exact action, ordered targets, counts, and wait timeout through restart; child current views replace only the parent Subagent inventory and never enter the root thread list; admitted child mutations do not perform post-effect List, View, or title calls, user Stop atomically records a terminal aborted turn and seals late provider, tool, and save-point work, canonical terminal items replace stream-only text without appending run-level output, stale canonical snapshots cannot replace a newer terminal view, canonical queue and interaction acceptance precedes visible success, unknown effects fail once and cannot be replayed, delete and shutdown fence active subtrees and effect dispatch, migration v2 through v9 remains atomic and fail-closed, verified fork context is rewritten to destination Thread identity without a downstream repair path, ordered views stay monotonic across live updates and restart, new tool history preserves complete Engine-authored call reasoning and hosted assistant fragment boundaries so source and fork continuation survive restart without duplicate calls; existing corrupt history is not rewritten, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access exists

Floret ThreadView.RunID, ThreadItem.RunID, ThreadInteraction.RunID, and RunProgress are the exact execution identity and phase source; Redeven does not infer historical run identity from the current run, TurnID, message content, or a parallel model-I/O stream

Floret v7.4.0 owns append-only canonical context plus full Turn-surface render lineages: forked context takes destination Thread identity from the canonical entry while preserving historical Turn and Run identity; Redeven freezes the persisted model, reasoning, System Prompt, tools, adapter, and context policy at new-Turn admission, treats request model fields only as consistency checks, keeps the original user objective in canonical history, appends mutable environment facts as per-turn supplemental context without rewriting an earlier request prefix, and starts each new context policy without the previous model's latest usage while preserving cumulative whole-thread totals
A natural provider stop completes a Flower Turn; ordinary tools continue, ask_user waits and resumes the same immutable surface, and settings or product-version changes affect only a later Turn

Provider history preserves ask_user as one Assistant tool call plus matching Tool result; public answers occur once in that result, secret values remain ephemeral, and provider-context v6 keeps typed historical tool facts stable across later Turns without restoring removed definitions or hashing runtime and journal entry identities

Floret v7.4.0 classifies invalid ask_user control calls as terminal control failures in live views, summaries, restart recovery, and provider history; historical waiting plus control_error facts cannot create pending input, and their Assistant calls receive one safe matching error Tool result without exposing arguments or validation details; Flower rejects missing, null, or empty typed questions before ThreadCache and retains one retryable Composer-adjacent sync error until a valid converged Current View arrives

Historical tool Activity is projected from persisted canonical presentation without consulting the current registry; removed tools use one neutral safe presentation and are not restored as compatibility definitions

Every Floret Run transition publishes the new exact RunID in preparing before provider dispatch and resets attempt ownership; Redeven forwards preparing, waiting_response, streaming, reasoning, and assistant growth directly without polling, inferred progress, or terminal backfill

Floret v7.4.0 publishes an unresolved approval or user-input interaction together with the matching active projection in one transition: waiting interactions clear run_progress while other active summaries retain it; local waiters are reserved before durable admission so response handling resumes the existing execution without duplicate provider dispatch
Floret ThreadService is the only lifecycle boundary for View, Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, PromoteQueued, and Subscribe
Each Floret thread has one in-memory ThreadRuntime owner; its canonical journal is the only durable lifecycle fact source
Redeven persists only product settings, authorization audit, uploads, read state, and the contiguous v1-to-v2 migration import boundary
Redeven handlers authorize and map typed requests without admission receipts, authority barriers, recovery handles, or projection mirrors
Flower uses one workspace SSE, summary/detail-separated ThreadCache, ComposerDraftStore, short-lived IndexedDB TransportOutbox, and LiveTransport
Thread selection never owns execution or reconnects transport; summary updates never overwrite typed detail
Unknown irreversible tool effects terminate their Turn with effect_outcome_unknown and have no replay or retry surface

Redeven consumes only published Flowersec Go and Core v5.0.1 plus Floe Webapp v0.48.5 for the Desktop shell and v0.48.6 for Env App, with exact module checksums and no replace, file, link, workspace, portal, sibling checkout, private import, or copied transport implementation

Public Local UI uses independent HTTPS and Flowersec WSS listeners with exact Host and Origin admission, one-shot artifacts, isolated concurrent windows, explicit terminal failure, and cleanup of pending authorization, handlers, sessions, and notification sinks; the private Desktop document bridge instead uses the isolated flowersec-private-loopback/1 browser and Go APIs behind exact numeric-loopback and per-process bridge-token admission

Each remote or local accepted session registers the final Flowersec SessionHandlers, RPC, ByteStream, and terminal/live_v1 boundaries directly; outbound terminal notification sinks attach to the established Flowersec RPC peer and detach idempotently when that session ends

Desktop attach and start, CA-free private bridge health, optional public device CA trust, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH runtime bootstrap, independent public WSS, terminal history recovery, and consecutive Desktop bridge sessions remain covered by focused transport contracts

Flowersec ConnectionController remains the only reconnect owner; secure-session retry uses Floe Webapp replaceConnection so an old asynchronous close cannot overwrite a new controller generation, while Redeven supplies artifact acquisition, authorization, permissions, product RPC handlers, and post-session business recovery without a second reconnect state machine or alternate carrier path

Runtime Service protocol_version is redeven-runtime-v2 at compatibility_epoch 10; Desktop verifies Runtime Service, the redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1 private bridge, Catalog, Local UI, package identity, and a unique managed process before a direct lifecycle operation succeeds
Gateway is an optional access component and never prepares, starts, stops, updates, reinstalls, or supervises a managed Runtime
